ai_executive_summary: We are pivoting to 'Aggressive Identification'—content so relatable that viewers feel personally attacked, forcing them to share it in their group chats to validate their own 'glitches'. By stripping away all academic tone, we turn every Short into a social-proof mirror that demands engagement.
self_learning_reflection: Abstract science fails because it creates 'distance' between the viewer and the screen; our new strategy closes that gap by focusing on things the viewer physically feels (twitches, memory gaps) or emotionally argues about (sports/regional biases).
recommended_topics_to_produce: The 50km 'Weather Wall': Why your weather app lies to you when you cross from the Kerala jungle into the Karnataka rain shadow, and why it feels like driving onto a different planet.
The 'Hidden' Cricket Rule that ruined your favorite team: Why the 'Mankad' dismissal is the most controversial play in sports and why 'spirit of the game' is just a cope for losing.
The 'Phantom Vibration' Glitch: Why your thigh 'feels' your phone buzzing when it's not even in your pocket, and why your brain is technically hallucinating a notification.
infinite_loop_directive: End the video by asking, 'Have you felt this in the last 24 hours?' or 'Is your favorite team guilty of this?', ensuring the final frame loops perfectly into the hook by referencing the specific 'glitch' or 'rivalry' mentioned at the start.
debate_bait_strategy: Intentionally include a polarizing take (e.g., 'If you think X is fair, you’re just a biased fan') to force people to defend their stance in the comments section.
